Headline takeaways from the research (9 parallel deep-dives, 173 live source lookups):

- **AGY** turned out to be Google's **Antigravity CLI** — closed-source Go binary, structurally similar plugin layout to Claude Code's, but the multi-vendor model claim and the `agy plugin add owner/repo` marketplace syntax in your CLAUDE.md aren't confirmed in Google's own docs — they trace to third-party tooling built to mimic Claude Code's UX.
- **Claude Code** itself has shifted from assistant to platform: near-daily releases, three distinct multi-agent layers (subagents / Workflows / experimental Agent Teams), and two things worth acting on — a documented malicious-skill supply-chain problem in plugin marketplaces, and `Auto` becoming the default permission mode in August (with a widely-cited incident of it nuking a production RDS database via Terraform).
- **Kimi/GLM/Qwen under Claude Code** via `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` is officially supported (not a ToS gray area) and 5–15× cheaper per token — but Claude Code's native orchestration (subagents/Workflows/Agent Teams) is Anthropic-model-only, and non-Anthropic backends show more loop pathology in open-ended agentic work. Verdict: tier it — cheap models for bounded/high-volume work, Sonnet/Opus for anything touching native orchestration or high stakes.
- **opencode** (~200k stars) is the real vendor-neutral option (75+ providers, novel from-scratch Zig TUI) but has no native multi-agent orchestration yet.
- The genuinely novel **UI** trend isn't chat redesigns — it's agents becoming addressable objects (Zed's Threads Sidebar, Cursor's Agents Window, Copilot's `/fleet`, Claude Code's tmux-pane Agent Teams), almost all built on git worktrees underneath.

## 2. Remote/headless/API/CI access — Yes, documented and more built-out than expected

- **Server mode** (opencode.ai/docs/server): `opencode serve [--port] [--hostname] [--cors]` runs a standalone headless HTTP server with an OpenAPI 3.1 spec at `/doc`. TUI and CLI are just clients of this server; a `/tui` endpoint lets external tools drive the TUI remotely (this is what the IDE plugins use). Optional basic auth via `OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD`.
- **GitHub Actions integration** (opencode.ai/docs/github): official GitHub App (github.com/apps/opencode-agent) triggered by `/opencode` or `/oc` PR/issue comments, or on a cron/scheduled workflow. Can triage issues, push fixes, open PRs, do automated reviews — fully hands-off with a required `prompt` input for scheduled runs.
- **Sharing**: `/share` creates a shareable link hosted on opencode.ai's CDN; self-hosting shared pages is on the roadmap per the Enterprise docs but not shipped.
- No dedicated mobile app found in docs.

Sources: opencode.ai/docs/server, opencode.ai/docs/github (fetched 2026-08-23)

## 3. Concrete differentiators vs Claude Code (beyond model support)

- **Pay-per-use pricing via OpenCode Zen**: no markup beyond processing fees ("sell at cost"), auto-reload credits, several temporarily-free models. Contrasts with Claude Code's flat subscription tiers.
- **Enterprise per-seat pricing with zero token cost if you bring your own LLM gateway** — you pay only for seats, not tokens, when routing through your org's own infrastructure (opencode.ai/docs/enterprise).
- **Server-as-source-of-truth architecture**: TUI/CLI/IDE extension are all just clients talking to the same local server process, which is what enables the `/tui` remote-drive endpoint — a more decoupled architecture than Claude Code's model.
- IDE integration (VS Code/Cursor/Windsurf/VSCodium) is presented as "terminal split + context sharing," not a distinct plugin UI — less differentiated than hoped; no unique inline-diff/review-flow features found in docs.

Sources: opencode.ai/docs/zen, opencode.ai/docs/enterprise, opencode.ai/docs/ide (fetched 2026-08-23)

- **No dedicated marketplace** — plugins are either local files (`.opencode/plugins/` or `~/.config/opencode/plugins/`) or npm packages declared in `opencode.json`, auto-installed via Bun. An "ecosystem" page references community plugins but there's no `marketplace.json`-equivalent registry.
- **Hook system is broad**: ~30+ lifecycle events across command/file/installation/LSP/message/permission/server/session/todo/shell/tool/tui categories, including `tool.execute.before/after`. **No router can split billing within one live session — this is now verified, not just cautioned.** Claude Code only reads two env vars (`ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`), and both apply to the *whole process*. Every real router (including claude-code-router) and every real-world hybrid setup found redirects at the whole-session level, not per-request-by-model-name.

**cc-fleet's own README confirms exactly why the two-lane pattern I recommended is correct:** it works by spawning a genuinely separate child `claude` process per backend and explicitly clears Anthropic auth from that child's environment. Your lead process keeps subscription billing because it's an *isolated process*, not because anything routed selectively within one session. That's the real mechanism behind every working setup — there's no clever middle-ground.

**So the verified, practical answer to "how are others doing it":**
- **Two separate sessions/profiles** — one untouched default Claude Code on subscription, one with `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` pointed at Kimi/GLM/Qwen — coordinated externally via worktrees or a tool like Claude Squad/cc-fleet's process-isolation pattern. This is what real 2026 write-ups describe (toggling `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` between sessions), not live per-model interception.
- **A bonus lever that needs none of this risk:** Claude Code's native `model: opusplan` runs Opus for planning and Sonnet for execution within one subscription session — same-provider tiering, zero backend-switch risk, real savings on the planning-heavy portion of work.

Done. Two real fixes this round, not another cosmetic bump:

**Root cause of the tiny fonts:** the diagrams had `width: 100%`, which force-scales the whole SVG (including its text) down to fit whatever container width is available — so no matter what font-size I set, it kept shrinking on narrower viewports. Fixed properly: each SVG now has explicit `width`/`height` attributes matching its own coordinate system, renders at true intrinsic size, and sits in a container that scrolls horizontally if it doesn't fit — the same pattern the tables already use, and the only way to guarantee text never shrinks below its authored size.

**Rounded corners:** yes, you're right — added `rx: 7px` to every rectangle in every diagram (one CSS rule, since `rx` is a stylable SVG property), and bumped every card/callout/signal/table/figure container from 2–4px to 10–14px radius, with tags and pills going fully rounded.
